newsitem.title: UK: OPEC reduces estimate for call on crude next year.
newsitem.headline: OPEC reduces estimate for call on crude next year.

text.p: OPEC's Vienna-based Secretariat in a monthly report revised down its estimate for world demand on OPEC crude next year by 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 24.9 million, OPEC news agency said.
The report said the Secretariat says the call on OPEC crude in 1997 is likely to remain unchanged from this year, despite world rising demand.

"An upward revision in non-OPEC supply of 200,000 bpd has led to a downward revision in the balance for OPEC oil in 1997 to 24.90 million bpd, compared with 25.10 million bpd in last month's report," said OPECNA.
"This balance is the same as that of 1996, which means that there will be no additional oil available for OPEC, despite the expected demand growth of 1.5 million bpd for 1997," the report said.
"That is, the growth in demand will be matched by similar growth in non-OPEC supply."
OPEC headquarters said it now projected average non-OPEC supply at 45.74 million bpd next year, 280,000 bpd higher than in last month's preliminary estimate and up from 44.26 million bpd in 1996.
The Secretariat forecasts global demand for 1997 at 70.63 million bpd, up 1.5 million or 2.2 percent from this year's 69.12 million and unchanged from last month's report.
Non-OPEC output in the fourth quarter of 1996 is expected to rise to 45.22 million bpd from 44.40 million in the third quarter.
OPEC crude production in August, according to direct communication from member countries, averaged 24.72 million bpd, down 100,000 bpd from July.
Supply to the market was 24.55 million bpd, lower by 60,000 bpd than in July.
Secondary media sources monitored by OPEC, including Reuters, put OPEC August production at 25.77 million bpd, 20,000 bpd more than in July, the report said.
